MEMORANDUM
  Agenda Item #: 3
  Meeting Date: 2-9-2021

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS

THRU:  LAURA GUGLIELMO, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  BRIANNA RINDGE, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE
  FOR JANUARY 14, 2021

DATE:  FEBRUARY 9, 2021

ACTION REQUIRED  CONSENT  X  RECEIVE & FILE

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council approve the actions of the Parklands Committee
for the meeting of January 14, 2021.

Summary

In the Parklands Committee meeting of January 14, 2021, all committee members were
present. The Committee discussed three applications: two for tree removal and one for tree
topping and recommended approval of all three with conditions.

Analysis and Findings

1. PC-546-21; Application to remove three Eucalyptus trees located in the Parklands
  adjacent to 2549 Via La Selva

Applicant: Kent Krekorian, 1516 Espinosa Circle, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

The applicant requests removal of three Eucalyptus trees growing in the Parklands to
enable a new electric service panel to be installed at 2549 Via La Selva. Removal of the
trees is required by California Edison before the job can be performed. No alternative
alignment would allow compliance according to the applicant.
  1
 The Committee supported the application for tree removal and agreed it was necessary for
safety and would have little impact to the Parklands. The Committee recommended waiver
of contribution to the Tree Bank due to the nature of the safety work.

Committee member Rhodes motioned and Cooper seconded (5-0 in favor) to recommend
approval to the City Council to remove three Eucalyptus trees adjacent to 2549 Via La
Selva for safety reasons, and:
  1. Require removal of the stumps only on the surface to protect the other tree roots in
  the area;
  2. Require a Tree Removal Permit issued by the City of Palos Verdes Estates; and
  3. Waive the contribution to the Tree Bank.

2. PC-547-21; Application to top one hedge of trees located adjacent to 1501 Via
  Lopez

Applicant: Scott Martin, 1061 Victoria Ave, Venice, CA 90291

The applicant requested topping to improve the view from the home under construction at
1412 Via Fernandez. The hedge consists of a mixture of public trees and tree branches
growing from private trees beyond the 12’ parkway.

The Urban Forester reviewed pictures from the main viewing areas in the home and each
image conveyed obstruction at some level. The trees are 200’ from the home and
approximately 42’ feet tall. All the trees were unpermitted and were never the Designated
Street Tree for this location.

Staff noted that the 10’ reduction was within arboricultural standards for trimming hedges
and would not yield safety issues. In some areas where this hedge could be trimmed, taller
private trees exist beyond which will limit the improvement, but the two largest ficus trees
at either end of the hedge would provide the most view enhancement.

The neighbor at 1501 Via Lopez indicated that his privacy would be impacted with more
than 5’ of reduction. Staff showed four pictures from 1501 Via Lopez indicating homes
above that would become more visible from the balcony of this neighbor.

The Committee members expressed concerned for potential privacy impacts but could not
quantify the amount or determine the effect due to the private trees behind the hedge. They
were also concerned about any possible liability when trimming branches of private trees
that extend into the public parkway.

Committee member Cooper motioned and Groves seconded (5-0 in favor) to recommend
approval to the City Council to top the hedge with conditions:
  1. Approve trimming to reduce all public ficus and public Podocarpus trees in the
  hedge to 32’ above grade;
  2. Require the trimming to be performed in the spring season;

  2
   3. Require the Urban Forester to direct the first topping with a Tree Topping Permit
  obtained by the applicant from the City; and
  4. Require the applicant to return to the Parklands Committee without a fee for review
  before annual trimming can be considered.

3. PC-548-21; Application to remove two Italian stone pines and one Eucalyptus
  located in the parkway adjacent to 2304 Paseo Del Mar and waive the planting of
  the Designated Street Tree

Applicant: Johnny and Carol Hong, 1544 Addison Road, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

The applicants request to remove three trees that will block their view from the main
viewing areas in their new home approved by Planning Commission at 2304 Paseo Del
Mar. The Urban Forester indicated that Italian stone pine trees cannot be topped without
damaging or killing the trees. The view from the first floor is under, through, and around
the trunk and branches of the existing trees. The approved second floor would always have
limited view over the trees due to the limits of pine tree trimming.

The neighbor at 2408 Paseo Del Mar supported the application while a couple of nearby
residents supported maintaining the trees for neighborhood character. Neither the applicant
nor the neighbor supported replanting with the Designated Street Tree as required by the
Neighborhood Compatibility standard conditions of approval.

The applicants argued that the Parklands Committee does not always require planting of
the Designated Street Tree when allowing removal. Staff reviewed the list of examples
provided by the applicants and noted planting street trees is a condition that was required
by the Planning Commission. Planting street trees to replace removed trees may be
required but is not always required by the Parklands Committee. The standard condition
of approval by Planning Commission affords the Parklands Committee opportunity to
modify the requirements related to trees within public right-of-way. Staff reviewed the list
provided by the applicant as follows.
  1. 2609 Via Rivera: not possible to replant due to the limited space and the location
  of the driveway
  2. 2765 Via Campesina: not possible to replant due to the limited space and location
  of the driveway.
  3. 2920 Via Pacheco: two existing olive trees were being crowded by the Jacaranda
  tree requested for removal so there was no space available to plant the Designated
  Street Tree.
  4. 2917 Via Rivera: across the street from the applicant therefore yielding
  maintenance issues.
  5. 1217 Via Romero: below and across the street from the applicant therefore yielding
  maintenance issues.
  6. 709 Paseo Del Mar: adjacent to the applicant; the Committee required payment to
  the Tree Bank; replanting of the Designated Street Tree possible but not required
  by the Parklands Committee.

  3
 The Committee agreed that the existing trees would block views from the home but only a
few members supported removing all three trees and/or Designated Street Tree planting
waiver. Keeping one appropriately placed tree was deemed problematic without
redesigning the driveway. Eliminating all street trees was rejected by a majority of the
Committee.

Committee member Groves motioned and Cooper seconded (3-2, in favor, Richie-Bray
and McCabe dissenting) to recommend approval to the City Council to remove two Italian
stone pine trees and one Eucalyptus tree:
  1. According to the “Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals”;
  2. Allow the trees to remain until the home is built;
  3. Require a Tree Removal Permit issued by the City;
  4. Require a Tree Bank contribution of $1500; and
  5. Require planting of at least one Kentia palm.

Notification

These matters have been agenized and posted in the routine manner.

Carl Moritz
Urban Forester
